parts.text:
35 A wire of cross-sectional area 5.0 × 10–6
m2 is made of a metal of resistivity 50 × 10–8
Ω m.
The potential difference across the wire is 6.0 V and the current is 3.0 A.
What is the length of the wire?
A
0.050 m
B
0.20 m
C
5.0 m
D
20 m

hints: First find the wire resistance from the given $6.0 \text{ V}$ and $3.0 \text{ A}$ using $R = V/I$.
Recall $R = \rho L / A$ links the $50 \times 10^{-8} \text{ } \Omega \text{ m}$ resistivity and $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$ area to length $L$.
Rearrange to $L = RA/\rho$, then substitute $R$ in $\Omega$, $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $\rho$ in $\Omega \text{ m}$ and check powers of 10.
walkthrough: Find resistance from the electrical measurements: $R = V/I = 6.0/3.0 = 2.0 \text{ } \Omega$.
State the resistivity relation: $R = \rho L / A$, where $\rho = 50 \times 10^{-8} \text{ } \Omega \text{ m}$ and $A = 5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$.
Simplify: numerator is $10 \times 10^{-6} = 1.0 \times 10^{-5}$, denominator is $5.0 \times 10^{-7}$, so $L = 20 \text{ m}$ with unit $\Omega \text{ m}^2 / \Omega \text{ m} = \text{m}$.

A.explanation: Gives $0.050 \text{ m}$ if $\rho$ and $A$ are inverted in $R = \rho L / A$ or powers of 10 are mishandled.

B.explanation: Gives $0.20 \text{ m}$ from an error of a factor of 100 in combining $10^{-6}$ and $10^{-8}$.

C.explanation: Gives $5.0 \text{ m}$ if resistance is taken as $0.50 \text{ } \Omega$ instead of $V/I = 2.0 \text{ } \Omega$.
